requirements.selectedText: If `id` is omitted, the authority allocates one.
`created` and `updated` carry `resource`, the complete Resource record as a `GET` of its URL would now return it
Applying the properties patch must yield a JSON object satisfying every effective Type schema. The metadata patch must yield a JSON object.
A semantic no-op update, defined under [Mutation revisions and guards](#mutation-revisions-and-guards), succeeds with outcome `updated` and the retained revision.
`propertiesChange` targets `properties` and `metadataChange` targets common `metadata`; each JSON Pointer is relative to its own complete object.
`add` has RFC 6902 object replacement and array insertion/append semantics.
A root-pointer `replace` with `{}` clears either object, including common `metadata`.
A Resource update can apply one to `properties`, one to common `metadata`, or both atomically.
If both results equal their respective preceding objects under RFC 6902 Section 4.6 JSON comparison, the operation is a no-op.
a write whose `properties` and common `metadata` changes are both no-ops mints no revision and records no new provenance and retains the existing version’s entire envelope.
The authority validates the complete `properties` result — not merely its changed members — against every effective Type contract; `metadata` has no Type schema.
The metadata patch must yield a JSON object.

An explicit update or deletion may supply `expectedRevision`: the revision observed by an earlier read or mutation result. The authority applies the operation only if the Resource still has that revision. A mismatch fails the individual operation without changing state. Omitting `expectedRevision` applies the change to the Resource's current state.
`revision-mismatch`: the member's `expectedRevision` is not the Resource's current revision.
The request executes as a one-operation Mutation Transaction.
Singleton operation targets on a Transactional Scope use exactly these statuses and rules
It carries the code's `status` — the HTTP status the failure would have had as a direct response, required because the enclosing status is `200 OK` — and `operationIndex`
the problem carries `pointer`, an RFC 6901 JSON Pointer into the request body as submitted
A `validation-failed` problem carries `diagnostics` and, when it truncated them, `diagnosticsTruncated`
The recorded `requiredPosition` remains evidence about the original view; it is not a valid minimum-read checkpoint for the replacement view.
The three Transactional response fields on a receipt or page response are the serving request's own observation, never the body's history
Receipt and receipt-page representations MUST omit `ETag` and `Last-Modified` initially and retain `Cache-Control: private, no-store`.

requirements.selectedText: The service rejects forward references, unknown names, duplicate names, and Resource-kind mismatches.
A batch request carries exactly one required `Idempotency-Key` HTTP field; the JSON body does not repeat it.
A body-level `idempotencyKey`, a per-operation `idempotencyKey`, or any other undefined member makes the request malformed.
A syntactically invalid request therefore never consults key state, and a retained or pending duplicate negotiates its receipt representation before limits and rate limits are evaluated
The receipt contains no committed operation results because the complete transaction is rolled back. Retrying returns that same failed receipt.
